  🧠 Project Focus: SMART Questions
Based on your earlier message, your project investigates:
  
  Can earnings be predicted by field of study, degree level, and aid profile?
  
  Do high Pell Grant programs lead to systematically lower earnings?
  
  Do online programs yield different earnings than in-person ones?
  
  🧭 Step-by-Step Strategy
✅ 1. Data Import
Import the original College Scorecard Field of Study dataset

Ensure earnings and aid variables are properly loaded as numeric

✅ 2. Data Cleaning
Select only relevant variables (earnings, Pell %, degree type, delivery mode, field name)

Convert character columns to numeric where needed

Handle missing values as appropriate

✅ 3. Exploratory Data Analysis (EDA)
Plot distributions of earnings overall and by subgroup:
  
  By major (field of study)

By credential level

By Pell Grant level

By delivery mode (distance vs in-person)

✅ 4. Statistical Testing and Modeling (Later)
T-tests, ANOVA, or regression to answer your questions quantitatively

#📊 SMART Q1: Can earnings be predicted by field, degree, and aid?
```{r}

```
```{r}
grep("earn", names(field_data), value = TRUE, ignore.case = TRUE)
```
Pull Aid Info from institute_data
```{r}

# Extract aid-related info from institution-level data
aid_vars <- institute_data %>%
  select(UNITID, PCTPELL, PCTFLOAN) %>%
  mutate(
    PCTPELL = as.numeric(PCTPELL),
    PCTFLOAN = as.numeric(PCTFLOAN)
  )

# Merge into field-level data
field_clean <- field_data %>%
  select(UNITID, EARN_MDN_1YR, CREDLEV, CIPDESC, DISTANCE) %>%
  left_join(aid_vars, by = "UNITID") %>%
  mutate(
    EARN_MDN = as.numeric(EARN_MDN_1YR),
    CREDLEV = factor(CREDLEV),
    DISTANCE = factor(DISTANCE, levels = c(0, 1), labels = c("In-Person", "Online"))
  ) %>%
  filter(!is.na(EARN_MDN))


```
📊 Earnings by Credential Level

```{r}
library(ggplot2)

ggplot(field_clean, aes(x = CREDLEV, y = EARN_MDN)) +
  geom_boxplot(fill = "lightblue") +
  labs(title = "Earnings by Credential Level", x = "Credential Level", y = "Median Earnings (USD)") +
  theme_minimal()

```

📊 Earnings by Major (Top 10 Most Frequent)
```{r}
top_majors <- field_clean %>%
  count(CIPDESC, sort = TRUE) %>%
  slice_head(n = 10) %>%
  pull(CIPDESC)

ggplot(field_clean %>% filter(CIPDESC %in% top_majors), 
       aes(x = CIPDESC, y = EARN_MDN)) +
  geom_boxplot(fill = "tan") +
  labs(title = "Earnings by Major (Top 10 Fields)", x = "Field of Study", y = "Earnings") +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1)) +
  theme_minimal()

```
📉 Scatter: Pell Grant % vs Earnings
```{r}
ggplot(field_clean, aes(x = PCTPELL, y = EARN_MDN)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.5, color = "darkgreen") +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", color = "black") +
  labs(title = "Pell Grant % vs Earnings", x = "% Pell Grant", y = "Earnings") +
  theme_minimal()

```
-SMART Question 2 Do high Pell Grant programs earn less?
  ```{r}
# grouping
field_clean <- field_clean %>%
  mutate(pell_group = ifelse(PCTPELL >= 0.5, "High Pell", "Low Pell"))

ggplot(field_clean, aes(x = pell_group, y = EARN_MDN, fill = pell_group)) +
  geom_boxplot() +
  labs(title = "Earnings by Pell Grant Group", x = "Pell Grant Level", y = "Median Earnings") +
  theme_minimal()


```

Do online programs differ in earnings?
  
  Online vs In-Person
```{r}
ggplot(field_clean, aes(x = DISTANCE, y = EARN_MDN, fill = DISTANCE)) +
```

## ANOVA by credential Level
```{r}
anova_credlev <- aov(EARN_MDN ~ CREDLEV, data = field_clean)
summary(anova_credlev)

```
Significant
```{r}
TukeyHSD(anova_credlev)
```

2. ANOVA: Earnings by Pell Group (High vs Low)
```{r}
anova_pell <- aov(EARN_MDN ~ pell_group, data = field_clean)
summary(anova_pell)

```
3. ANOVA: Earnings by Distance Mode
```{r}
anova_dist <- aov(EARN_MDN ~ DISTANCE, data = field_clean)
summary(anova_dist)

```



Step 1: Define a Regression Model
We can’t fully isolate causal effects without an experimental design or instrumental variable, but we can control for observable confounders to reduce bias.

Model Idea:
  r
Copy
Edit
EARN_MDN ~ PCTPELL + CREDLEV + DISTANCE + PCTFLOAN + CIPDESC
This model attempts to control for differences in:
  
  Degree type (CREDLEV)

Program delivery (DISTANCE)

Debt and aid status (PCTFLOAN)

Major (CIPDESC) — as a fixed effect if treated as a factor

```{r}
# Fit linear regression with fixed effects for field of study
model <- lm(EARN_MDN ~ PCTPELL + PCTFLOAN + CREDLEV + DISTANCE + CIPDESC, data = field_clean)
summary(model)

```
